metadata.description: Perf interaction helper: drag a target horizontally by dx over stepped pointer moves (mousedown → stepped mousemove → mouseup). Use it to exercise resize handles / draggable dividers whose lag you are auditing. Stepped moves settle transition queues so resize-lag traces reproduce.

labels.parameters_json: [{"name":"selector","type":"string","required":true,"description":"CSS selector of the drag handle (use a literal [data-testid=...]; @selector tokens do not resolve on the capture path)"},{"name":"dx","type":"number","required":false,"default":80,"description":"Horizontal drag distance in pixels"},{"name":"steps","type":"number","required":false,"default":20,"description":"Number of intermediate pointer moves"}]

metadata.name: perf-drag-horizontal

evaluate.expression: (() => { const el = document.querySelector("${@params/selector}"); if (!el) throw new Error('perf-drag-horizontal: ${@params/selector} not found'); const dx = Number("${@params/dx}") || 80; const steps = Math.max(1, Number("${@params/steps}") || 20); const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); const sx = r.left + r.width / 2, sy = r.top + r.height / 2; const fire = (type, x) => el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent(type, { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, clientX: x, clientY: sy, buttons: type === 'mouseup' ? 0 : 1 })); fire('mousedown', sx); for (let i = 1; i <= steps; i++) { fire('mousemove', sx + (dx * i) / steps); } fire('mouseup', sx + dx); return true; })()
